page.layout: Running head at top across the page: "THEOD. BEZÆ" (one block, full width). Below it a heading "Auiculæ Acanthidi." Then one block of verse in one column of italic lines with a large initial E at left; no margin notes; no page number; no catchword.

main_text.l: ERgo etiam innocua Mors insidiata Volucri

l.i: Guttur quo nullum resonantes purius auras
Guttur quo nullum teretes demulserat aures
iue graui, seu voce melos resonaret acuta,
AEterno infelix (ah fata, ah aspera fata)
Non igitur deinceps, mea dulcis auicula, tecum
Nec Domini digitu multo cum murmure pugę
Nec Domini subito blando pacata fusurro,
Nec lucem arguta venientem voce salutans,
Nec te cunctarum volucrum referente canores,
Finieris igitur, mea dulcis auicula, postquam
Quin potius numeris numeros penfabo vicissim,

page.notes: Initial E is a large decorative letter. Long s printed as f in places was transcribed as s. Several line-initial words are marked by small decorative marks (e.g. before "Non", "Nec", "Finieris") that are not text. Some words at the right edge (e.g. "Volucri", "canores", "Sicissim") may be cut off by the scan edge; the letter "ꝯ"-type abbreviation in "vicissim" is read as printed. Lines near the right edge are partly cropped.
